title: Chapter 32: I Cried and Screamed and Will Cry No More
content:
Chapter 32:

I Cried and Screamed and Will Cry No More

“Welcoming a peaceful sleep on a girl’s lap while having my head stroked… Looked at on its own, it was an absolutely supreme event, but still.”

Scratching his head, Subaru muttered that with an awkward face.

Casting his eyes down, his profile biting back sighs over and over, while increasing the speed of the hand scratching his head, red all the way to his ears,

“In front of the girl I have feelings for, crying and wailing super hard, complaining, my face a complete mess of tears and snot, and falling fast asleep. On top of that, monopolizing that girl’s lap for hours in that state… just what kind of humiliation play is this anymore.”

What he recalled was the sensation of Emilia’s lap, and the disastrous state her lap must have been in, brought about by Subaru sleeping heavily for hours.

It was in a terrible state with tears, drool, snot, and other things, a state that could not be overlooked purely from a hygiene standpoint, let alone from the standpoint of Subaru’s boy-index.

Despite this, she didn’t spontaneously try to shake Subaru awake until he woke up on his own, and despite having her clothes dirtied like that, she didn’t do anything like blame Subaru when he woke up apologizing profusely.

“If you were able to rest even a little, that’s fine. Besides, Subaru, you don’t understand.”

“Huh?”

“Rather than being told ‘I’m sorry’ over and over, if you just say ‘Thank you’ once at times like this, the other person will be satisfied. I didn’t do it because I wanted you to apologize, I did it because I wanted to do it for you.”

Was there a man out there who wouldn’t be completely smitten when a finger was placed on his lips as he voiced an apology, and she said that while winking one eye? No, there was not.

In fact, Subaru fell completely and easily. He was head over heels for her to begin with, so having the final nail driven in multiplied his affection.

Parting ways with Emilia, who left saying she was going to change her clothes, he wandered the mansion unsteadily in a dreamlike mood for a while, and when he came to his senses, this was the state he was in.

Looking back on his own deeds today, the unsightliness of it made him want to cry. Since he had cried so much after that, he couldn’t shed any tears now, though.

“I’m hopeless—I’m super hopeless—. What do I mean ‘I only want to hide my weak side from Emilia-tan,’ I’ve shown her my most shameful side ever. I seriously can’t even face you anymore after this—”

“…Sneaking into someone’s room late at night, and that’s what you start saying, I suppose. Just when it was seemingly peaceful because you were nowhere to be seen all day, it’s an unwanted disaster, in fact.”

Sitting on the middle step of a stepladder, Beatrice cursed, casting a sidelong glance at Subaru, who was writhing near the entrance.

Wandering around the mansion, brooding that he absolutely couldn’t face the others while sober, the place Subaru headed to was this forbidden small room out of anyone’s reach. Though, for the young girl who was its master, it must have been highly dissatisfying.

However, that wasn’t the only reason he came here.

Don’t say that, Beako. It’s just us, right?”

“What kind of relationship exists between Betty and you… Wait, in fact. Before that, what did you just call Betty, I wonder?”

Raising one eyebrow, Beatrice questioned with her cheek twitching. Subaru clapped his hands at her attitude and,

“Ah, 

Beako.

1

 For someone I feel a certain degree of intimacy with, a nickname. I think this is necessary. Until now, among the people in the mansion, I never felt that kind of feeling towards anyone but you, but…”

What he was recalling was the time during the previous loop, right when he was completely steeped in despair.

Even if it wasn’t a situation where she had been smooth-talked into it from her perspective, there had certainly been a contract exchanged between the two of them.

Beatrice had dutifully kept it, and had even gone out of her way to vaguely word the contract to help Subaru.

Even if she had completely forgotten, there was no way he could forget the feeling of being saved at that time.

Therefore,

“No matter what you think of me, I will call you Beako. That’s the utmost proof of affection I can give you—!”

“Betty’s absolutely not happy about it, in fact! What is with this pushy goodwill, I suppose! Rather than disgusting, it makes me sick to my stomach, in fact!”

“What’s with that way of speaking! I’m seriously trying to convey my heartfelt gratitude here, this isn’t a scene you can just make fun of!”

“If you can look back at what you just said and tell me you weren’t joking, then what’s established between you and Betty anymore isn’t a conversation, but something else that feels like a conversation, in fact!”

Subaru, intending to challenge her to a game of conversational catch, was told he got the sport wrong and was playing kabaddi, and he stuttered.

It was Subaru’s own way of expressing affection, but unfortunately, it seemed it didn’t quite resonate with her heart. Honestly disappointed by that, he involuntarily hung his head despondently.

“Well, setting that aside, I’m still gonna keep calling you Beako, though.”

“Such unnecessary devotion, in fact. Then Betty will absolutely never respond even if called by such a name, I suppose. With that, our opinions are in agreement, in fact.”

“Don’t say such cold things, Beako.”

“…”

However, to Subaru’s call, Beatrice remained silent, keeping her eyes dropped to her book and not responding. It seemed she intended to put her previous statement into practice.

Approaching the stubborn girl, Subaru walked in circles around the stepladder and,

“Beako Beako Beako Beako Beako Beako Beako Beako Beako…”

“—You’re unparalleled in your annoyance, in fact! What is your problem, I suppose!!”

He chanted her name repeatedly as if playing kabaddi. Beatrice’s emotions, having been continuously whispered into her ear, reached boiling point, and Subaru struck a triumphant fist pump, having achieved his objective.

Then, turning back to her once more, he twisted the corner of his mouth at the girl who was still squaring her shoulders in anger,

“I’m cornered and blocked on all sides. To be blunt, I want to borrow your help.”

—Having wept unseemly, having lost his composure to an unsightly degree, he told the girl with twin drills the conclusion he had reached at the end of it all.

※※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※

Spitting out his true feelings on Emilia’s lap, having completely washed away the dirty feelings he had bottled up and the tears he couldn’t hold back, what remained inside Subaru was purely his own greed.

He liked Emilia. He liked the life in the mansion where he could spend time with her. He liked the environment where he could learn various things. He liked Ram, who took care of him in various ways despite being blunt. He super liked Emilia. He liked Rem, who guided him while subtly insulting him in polite language. Emilia-tan was seriously a goddess. He owed a debt of gratitude to Roswaal, who provided this paradise-like situation. He had received a favor from Beatrice that he could no longer fully repay. He harbored affection for the people living in this mansion that he could not throw away. He could not bring himself to throw away the happiness of being there.

Thoughts overflowed so profusely they caught in his chest.

The memories of happiness he couldn’t wipe away were the source of vitality moving Subaru.

However, while thinking that, on the other hand—

He liked Emilia. He felt pathetic for lacking the power to protect her. Life in the mansion left no room to relax. He didn’t know when they’d give up on him. Ram, who severed his leg with a blade of wind and pierced his neck, was terrifying. Rem, who repeatedly tortured him even while healing his wounds and crushed his skull with an iron ball, was horrifying. The fathomless madness of Roswaal, who kept those two and could presumably order Subaru’s execution without a shred of mercy on top of that, was disgusting. The time spent having to check if his life was still there every time he woke up, having to doubt if despair was creeping up on him, was unbearably painful and sad.

Those too were the true feelings inside Subaru that would not disappear.

The conflicting emotions could not tolerate each other’s existence, and Subaru was spending a time of living and struggling while harboring them on his surface and in his heart.

A time where he had to keep smiling as if walking barefoot on thin ice, without even showing a hint that the skin on the soles of his feet was peeling off.

Emilia did not overlook Subaru’s agony, the miserable anguish of resisting despair, and scooped it up.

Perhaps it was Puck who noticed. For that spirit who could read minds, he would have easily seen through the clumsy mask Subaru wore.

But even so, it was Emilia who comforted Subaru’s heart, his heart that was on the verge of wearing out.

He didn’t care if this was dependency.

There was not a shred of doubt that the driving force moving Subaru’s heart right now was his feelings for her.

Yes, in other words—

“Emilia-tan is seriously an archangel.”

“Did you just spout something intensely stupid, I wonder?”

“Not at all. I just reaffirmed the most important thing to me.”

He could answer that confidently, puffing out his chest.

And being given full affirmation of his previous statement like that, Beatrice let out a sigh as if even making an exasperated gesture was a hassle,

“Let’s get back to the topic, in fact… So, about this matter of you asking for Betty’s help, I suppose.”

“Yeah, it’s seriously a feeling like praying to God. I can’t think of anyone else I can cling to.”

Currently, the person Subaru could place his absolute trust in within this mansion. That was, of course, Emilia, but her existence was simultaneously the most important factor for him.

In short, he didn't want her, if anyone, to face danger. For Subaru, whose own life was his highest priority, her existence was the one thing he could weigh against his life without hesitation.

Therefore, in this loop where a confrontation with the curse arts user was kept in mind, he did not want to choose the option of borrowing her help until the very bitter end.

That being so, it naturally became difficult to borrow the power of Puck, who was constantly by her side, and the remaining option was—.

“You’re actually a quite soft, easy-to-win-over Beako when it comes down to it, that’s what it means.”

“Even if the content isn't understandable, the insulting atmosphere can still be sensed, in fact?”

“I don’t have a speck of an intention like that… In reality, you’re the only one I can rely on in this mansion in the current situation.”

He obviously couldn’t confide in Ram or Rem, nor Roswaal. If there was anyone else Subaru could rely on right now in this mansion besides Emilia, it was none other than her.

“Please. —Like this, I’m begging you.”

That’s why Subaru knelt on the floor in front of her, bowed his head, and pleaded.

For her cooperation. For her to be the light that illuminated the path for him to draw the curtain on the repeating chain of despair.

“I need your power. Putting it all together, I want to protect the place where I can be happy.”

“————”

Keeping his head bowed deeply, a silent time fell between the two.

While waiting for a reply, Subaru’s heart pounded violently in his chest with anxiety. However, as the silence dragged on, that sound also gradually faded, and feeling suspicious, he shot a quick glance upward. Then,

“…Beatrice?”

Involuntarily, forgetting their exchange from just before, he called her by her name.

He was compelled to do so, because the expression with which Beatrice stared at Subaru was wavering with emotion filled with sorrow.

Furrowing her brows faintly, biting her lip, Beatrice was glaring at Subaru. She was glaring, but to him, it looked like a face that was about to burst into tears at any moment.

He swallowed his breath and waited silently for her next reaction.

Beatrice, taking her time as if to calm the wave of emotion that had risen inside her, kept her eyes closed and quietly,

“…There is no reason for Betty to comply with your demands, in fact.”

Returned only that feebly.

“Beako… I…”

“Silence, human. Betty won’t be gentle to you forever, in fact. If you’re getting carried away, you won’t be forgiven, I suppose.”

Interrupting Subaru, Beatrice rattled on rapidly.

Dumbfounded by the oversensitivity of her reaction, Subaru was surprised and confused as to what part of his previous statement had touched her heartstrings.

That likely only strengthened the stubbornness of the already uncooperative girl, and invited this worsening of the situation.

He intended to convey his sincerity, but it backfired.

A result he couldn’t regret enough, but Subaru didn’t possess a delicate mental structure to agonize over it now.

Doing something and having it backfire was a situation he was already completely used to under these circumstances. In this world he had repeated five times, had the dice he cast ever turned up a result good enough to even remember?

Once he thought that, he could crush any weak, smoldering heart he had. To begin with, he had already completely washed away his weak self, who would stop in his tracks over something like this, in a flood of snot and drool on Emilia’s lap.

He decided he hadn’t shed any tears. A man who cried not just in front of the girl he liked, but on her lap—such a man was the worst kind of man.

He had his pride, because he was a boy.

“Listen to me, Beatrice. I understand your feeling of wanting to push me away like that. From your perspective, I’m just some incomprehensible, rude bastard who was carried in just a day ago.”

“If you understand that much, you should understand Betty’s answer too, in fact.”

“It was you who closed the wound on my stomach, right? I’m grateful. You probably don’t know this, but I have a ton of things I have to be incredibly grateful to you for, and on top of that, I’m still up to my neck in trouble if I don’t rely on you. It’s pathetic. It’s hopelessly miserable. But, I only have you.”

As if folding over, he spat out all the words floating in his mind.

He was aware that it was a selfish claim, forcefully pushing his way through without showing the slightest consideration for her feelings, yet Subaru bowed his head.

Looking down at his incoherent words and his bowed figure, Beatrice gave a small snort like usual, and,

“Lamenting your lack of power, while unseemly groveling on the ground begging and clinging. Do you have no pride at all, I wonder?”

“I saw what’s important clearly. If smashing my head into the ground ten or a hundred times is enough, I’ll do it as many times as it takes.”

He didn’t possess the cheap pride to obsess over his own insignificance.

Keeping his head bowed, he persistently maintained his pleading posture.

He knew it was a cowardly method. In the world he had repeated five times, Subaru had met Beatrice many times, and had continued to argue with her each time.

Because she was an opponent with whom he had carried such a relationship with, he knew. The girl named Beatrice, even if she superficially took an attitude of pushing others away—.

“Raise your face, in fact.”

A somewhat resigned, gentle voice reached his ears, and Subaru thought his lowly plea had gotten through.

He recognized his own insignificance anew, and felt self-loathing at his insincere behavior that disguised itself as sincerity towards her. However, it was also a fact that it was a necessary process. He had to be pragmatic.

More than anything, he had to decide to use all available means to obtain the future he desired—.

“Bea…”

“Eat this, I suppose.”

“Bubeh.”

However, a hard object that suddenly approached was ruthlessly smashed into the face that had firmed up such a tragic resolve.

Only his neck tilted backwards while still in a dogeza posture, and as a result, an indescribable sound echoed through the Forbidden Library, and a voiceless scream reverberated.

Subaru writhed in agony, still bent backward like a shrimp.

Unable to comprehend the damage that assaulted his cervical spine, his gaze wandered as he agonized in pain, and his eyes met Beatrice’s, who was raising one leg with her arms crossed.

Comprehension. The girl had launched a merciless yakuza kick right into the face of the dogeza-ing Subaru.

“You… this…!”

“I can’t understand the simplemindedness of thinking that rolling around a hundred heads of someone like you would be commensurate with Betty’s effort, in fact. No matter how many copper coins you gather, you’ll never reach a single Holy Gold Coin. Learn that, I suppose.”

“No, even if it’s copper coins, if you gather thousands of them they’ll reach a Holy Gold Coin, right? If you’re comparing them in terms of value, that’s what it amounts to, you know!? Are you okay with math?”

“Stop looking at me with eyes like you’re looking at a pitiful child, I suppose! Those aren’t the eyes of someone who was trying to rely on Betty just a moment ago, in fact?!”

Squawking noisily, a war of words between Beatrice and Subaru began.

In the world he had repeated numerous times, an offense and defense that never started for the same reason even once.

While continuing the familiar argument with her, before he knew it, the tragic resolve that had been inside Subaru began to seem like something ridiculous.

After going through such an exchange, the conclusion of the war of words eventually was—.

“Alright, I’ll play my trump card. If you cooperate with me, I’ll endure taking your Mana Drain a few times.”

“Your mana doesn’t have as much value as you say, in fact. It certainly… um, perhaps we had good compatibility or it tasted better than normal mana, I suppose.”

“My mana has a track record of being sucked by Puck too. In other words, an indirect Mana Drain… You know what that means, right?”

Beatrice, whose face changed color, nodding while biting her lip in frustration against Subaru, who was steeped in the superiority of carrying the negotiation favorably, was the conclusion.

Looking back, Subaru thought it was a rather anticlimactic resolution.

Of course, by bringing it to such a flow, he reluctantly secured her cooperation.

—Although he knew that the little magician had arranged it that way for him.
